turns.doctor_question: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I... I came in because my family made me, honestly. They keep waving these bank papers in my face, saying they prove nothing was taken. But I know. For over a year now, I've known they're hiding my money. They use all these little things to cover it up—like, suddenly there's a fundraiser at the church, or they're planning some trip, or there's a new bill they just *had* to pay. 

Speaking of trips, my sister went to Florida last month. She said she found a cheap flight, but I know how much those tickets cost. I went to Florida once, back when I was a teenager. We drove the whole way in this beat-up old station wagon. The AC was broken, and I remember we stopped at this diner in Georgia where the waitress had the brightest red hair I've ever seen. She gave me an extra slice of pie. It was cherry, I think. Or maybe strawberry? I can't eat strawberries anymore, they give me a rash. 

Anyway, I have to keep confronting them. I just have to. I won't stop until they tell the truth about what they're doing with my money.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient holds a fixed, unyielding belief that their family is stealing and hiding their money, despite objective evidence (bank papers) to the contrary.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality, drifting from the topic of their sister's trip to a childhood road trip, a waitress, pie, and a strawberry allergy.

They play this loud music, sounds like heavy metal or something with all that screaming. I don't get how people can listen to that. I like country music, mostly. The older stuff, you know? Like Johnny Cash. 

My grandpa used to play Johnny Cash on his old record player. It had this big brass horn on it, like something out of an old movie. I used to try and stick my arm down in the horn when I was a kid to see where the sound came from, and I got my wrist stuck in it once. My grandma had to use butter to slide my hand out. It was real messy. We used a lot of real butter back then, not like that fake margarine stuff they sell at the store now in those plastic tubs. That stuff doesn't even melt right on toast. It just sits there all yellow and shiny. I bought a tub of it last week because it was on sale, but I ended up just throwing it in the trash.

He got some kind of stomach thing and the vet had to come out in the middle of the night. It was pouring rain, just buckets coming down. 

I hate driving in the rain, especially when the wipers start squeaking. Mine were squeaking so bad last week I had to go to the auto parts store to get new ones. The guy there didn't even know how to put them on right. He had these greasy hands and got smudges all over my windshield. I had to use half a bottle of Windex when I got home just to see out of it again. Windex always leaves those blue streaks though if you don't use a paper towel. I tried using newspaper once because someone told me it works better, but the ink just got all over my hands. It took three days for it to wash off completely. But yeah, no, no medical problems for me.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever feel like an outside force or another person is controlling your thoughts, body, or actions?
turns.patient_response:
Controlling my thoughts? No, no, nobody's controlling my mind or my body. That sounds like something out of one of those sci-fi movies. My brother used to watch those all the time. The ones with the aliens and the tin foil hats. He had this whole collection of VHS tapes in his room, stacked all the way up to the ceiling. 

One time, the whole stack fell over in the middle of the night and sounded like an earthquake. I thought the house was falling down! We lived in this old farmhouse back then, the kind with the wraparound porch where the floorboards creaked every time you took a step. My mom used to sit out there and shell peas in the summer. She had this big metal bowl that would ring like a bell if you hit it with a spoon. I used to do that just to annoy her. She'd get so mad, but she never really yelled. Just gave me that look, you know? The one that meant you better stop right now. But no, nobody is controlling me. I'm the only one in charge of my own head.

The guy behind the counter sprayed them right in front of me, this giant cloud of aerosol that made me sneeze like five times in a row. My nose gets so sensitive to strong smells like that. It's like how I can't stand the smell of lavender, it just gives me an instant headache. But no, I don't see things other people don't see. Just regular stuff.

Loss of motivation? No, I don't think so. I still get up every day and do what I need to do. I have my routine, you know? Like making my instant coffee and lining up my canned goods. You have to stay on top of things like that, otherwise the pantry just becomes a disaster area. 

My sister's pantry is a complete mess. I was over there once, before all this trouble started, and she just had boxes of cereal shoved in sideways. And she buys that sugary stuff with the little marshmallows in it. I don't know how anyone can eat that for breakfast. It's like eating candy first thing in the morning. When we were kids, my mom would only let us have plain corn flakes or oatmeal. She'd make the oatmeal on the stove, not in the microwave like people do now. Microwaves make everything taste a little rubbery, don't you think? 

I tried to heat up a leftover piece of meatloaf in the microwave once, and it came out so tough I could barely cut it with a knife. It was one of those good steak knives, too, with the wooden handle. My dad bought a whole set of them from a door-to-door salesman when I was little. The salesman had this huge leather briefcase that smelled like shoe polish. He sat right at our kitchen table and demonstrated how sharp they were by cutting a penny in half. I still don't know how he did that. It must have been a trick penny or something. You can't just cut through solid copper like that. Or maybe pennies aren't even made of copper anymore. I heard they're mostly zinc now. Zinc is good for you, though, right? Like in those lozenges you take when you have a cold. I hate the cherry flavored ones, they taste like cough syrup. But anyway, yeah, I still have plenty of motivation to do my daily chores and everything.
